stem.text: Let \( f(x) = \frac{\left(2 - 2 x\right) \left(x - 4\right)}{\left(x - 1\right) \left(x + 3\right)^{2}} \). Determine whether f is continuous at \( x = -3 \). If it is not, classify the discontinuity as removable, a jump, or a vertical asymptote. Justify your answer.

answer_key.label: The discontinuity at \( x = -3 \) is a vertical asymptote, because f(x) is unbounded as x approaches -3.

worked_solution.text: Factor and divide out the common factor: for \( x \ne 1 \), \( f(x) = \frac{8 - 2 x}{\left(x + 3\right)^{2}} \).
Near \( x = -3 \) the numerator of the reduced expression approaches 14 and the denominator approaches 0 through positive values, so \( \lim_{x \to -3} f(x) = \infty \).
worked_solution.rule_named: sign analysis of the reduced quotient

worked_solution.text: f is unbounded near the input, so the discontinuity is a vertical asymptote.

options.label: The discontinuity at \( x = -3 \) is a jump, because f is undefined there so the limit does not exist.
options.derivation: the limit declared nonexistent because f is undefined at the input, so the break called a jump

options.label: There is no discontinuity at \( x = -3 \), because the limits from the left and from the right are equal.
options.derivation: agreeing one sided limits, both infinite, taken as continuity

options.label: The discontinuity at \( x = -3 \) is removable, because the limit of f(x) there exists and equals \( \infty \).
options.derivation: the statement that the limit is infinite read as saying the limit exists, so the break called removable
